answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through length-bounded random walks, so a Sybil set \(S\) with low conductance, \(\phi(S)=\mathrm{cut}(S,V\setminus S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\), has limited walk flow across its boundary. When votes are weighted by propagated trust, the cluster’s aggregate weight is therefore constrained by external cut capacity and the seed distribution, not by the number of identities it creates. Saffron accounts may wander within the cluster, but cannot make it a haven without gaining attestations from outside.
